pages.narration_en: You've just moved to Porto. You're standing in the hall of São Bento Station, surrounded by blue-and-white azulejo tiles. Today is your AIMA appointment at the AIMA store on Avenida de França, but you don't know the way. A woman next to you smiles and greets you.

dead_ends.text_en: The woman raises an eyebrow: 'Cara? Que cara?' In Portugal 'cara' means 'face'. She laughs and helps you out.

side_scene.narration_en: The woman frowns, says 'Cara? Que cara?' and walks off toward the platforms, shaking her head with a smile. You look around the hall, a bit embarrassed. Another friendly woman nearby catches your eye and smiles.

pages.narration_en: The woman smiles: 'Sim?' Ask her where the bus stop is.

choices.text_pt: Onde fica a paragem do autocarro?
Onde fica o ponto de ônibus?
Onde fica a casa de banho?

dead_ends.text_en: The woman: 'Ah, do Brasil? Aqui é autocarro!' Not wrong, but here in Porto people speak European Portuguese.
dead_ends.reteach_pt: Onde fica a paragem do autocarro?

side_scene.narration_en: The woman smiles: 'Ah, do Brasil?' She starts telling you about her cousin in São Paulo. Ten minutes later, you know the whole family tree, but still not the way to the bus.

lines.speaker: senhora
lines.pt: Ah, do Brasil? A minha prima vive em São Paulo!
lines.en: Oh, from Brazil? My cousin lives in São Paulo!

lines.speaker: senhora
lines.en: Here we say autocarro and paragem.

dead_ends.text_en: She kindly walks you to the toilet. Nice, but now you're running late!
dead_ends.reteach_pt: Onde fica a paragem do autocarro?

side_scene.narration_en: She kindly walks you all the way to the station toilets and waits outside, proud to help. You come out and she's still there, beaming.

pages.narration_en: You reach the bus stop outside São Bento Station. A bus is waiting. You need to get to Avenida de França. Ask whether this bus goes there.

lines.speaker: senhora
lines.en: It's over there, on the right.

choices.text_pt: Este autocarro vai para a Avenida de França?
choices.text_en: Does this bus go to Avenida de França?

dead_ends.text_en: The driver says proudly: 'É lindo, sim!' and drives off. Wait for the next one.
dead_ends.reteach_pt: Este autocarro vai para a Avenida de França?
dead_ends.reteach_en: Does this bus go to Avenida de França?

side_scene.narration_en: The driver beams: 'É lindo, sim!' He pats the dashboard, closes the door and drives off, very happy. You wait for the next bus with a pigeon for company.

pages.narration_en: You arrive at the AIMA store (Loja AIMA) on Avenida de França. There's a security guard at the door.

lines.speaker: segurança
lines.en: Good morning. Do you have an appointment?

choices.text_pt: Sim, tenho um agendamento às dez.
choices.text_en: Yes, I have an appointment at ten.

dead_ends.text_en: The guard: 'Dez anos? Tem muita altura para dez anos!' (You're very tall for ten!)
dead_ends.reteach_en: I have an appointment at ten.

side_scene.narration_en: The guard looks you up and down, very seriously. 'Dez anos?' Then he bursts out laughing and calls a colleague over to share the joke.

lines.speaker: segurança
lines.pt: Dez anos? Tem muita altura para dez anos!
lines.en: Ten years old? You're very tall for ten!

lines.speaker: segurança
lines.pt: Tem agendamento às dez, não é?
lines.en: You have an appointment at ten, right?

pages.narration_en: The guard wants to see your appointment letter (convocatória).

lines.speaker: segurança
lines.en: Do you have the appointment letter?

choices.text_en: Yes, it's on my cell phone. (Brazilian)

dead_ends.text_en: The guard laughs: 'Celular? Aqui dizemos telemóvel.'

side_scene.narration_en: The guard tilts his head: 'Celular?' A man in the queue behind you joins in, and soon three people are teaching you the word.

lines.speaker: segurança
lines.en: Cell phone? Here we say telemóvel.

pages.narration_en: You're in the waiting room of the AIMA store. An older lady next to you starts chatting. Tip: with strangers use 'o senhor / a senhora'; 'tu' is informal.

lines.speaker: senhora
lines.pt: Está à espera há muito tempo? Parece {cansado}.
lines.en: Have you been waiting long? You look tired.

choices.text_pt: Estou a esperar há vinte minutos.
choices.text_en: I've been waiting for twenty minutes.
I've been waiting for twenty minutes. (Brazilian structure)

dead_ends.text_en: The lady: 'Esperando? Isso é do Brasil! Em Portugal: estou a esperar.'

side_scene.narration_en: The older lady gasps, then laughs and pulls a little notebook from her bag. She writes it down for you, very slowly, like a teacher.

pages.narration_en: Your number appears on the screen. You go to the counter (balcão).

lines.speaker: funcionária
lines.pt: Bom dia. O seu passaporte, se faz favor.

dead_ends.text_en: You hand over a croissant. The clerk: 'Obrigada, mas prefiro o passaporte.'

side_scene.narration_en: You reach into your bag and hand over... a croissant. The clerk stares at it, then smiles and pretends to take a tiny bite.

lines.speaker: funcionária
lines.en: Thank you, but I prefer the passport.

pages.narration_en: The clerk asks for proof of address. If you rent, a declaration from your landlord works. She speaks fast.

lines.speaker: funcionária
lines.en: Do you have proof of address?

choices.text_pt: Sim, tenho o comprovativo de morada.
choices.text_en: Yes, I have proof of address.

choices.text_pt: Pode falar mais devagar, por favor?
choices.text_en: Could you speak more slowly, please?

choices.text_pt: Sim, tenho uma morada muito bonita.
choices.text_en: Yes, I have a very pretty address.

dead_ends.text_en: Great sentence, this is a helpful side path, not a mistake! The clerk repeats slowly: 'Com-pro-va-ti-vo de mo-ra-da.' Now answer her.
dead_ends.reteach_pt: Sim, tenho o comprovativo de morada.
dead_ends.reteach_en: Yes, I have proof of address.

side_scene.narration_en: The clerk smiles and slows right down, one syllable at a time. The man at the next counter starts listening too.

dead_ends.text_en: The clerk: 'Que bom! Mas preciso do papel.' (How nice! But I need the paper.)
dead_ends.reteach_pt: Sim, tenho o comprovativo de morada.
dead_ends.reteach_en: Yes, I have proof of address.

side_scene.narration_en: The clerk's eyes light up. 'Muito bonita? Onde?' She asks about your street, your balcony, your view... and then gently holds out her hand for the paper.

lines.speaker: funcionária
lines.pt: Que bom! Mas preciso do papel.
lines.en: How nice! But I need the paper.

pages.narration_en: Now the biometrics: your photo. The clerk points at the camera.

lines.speaker: funcionária
lines.pt: Olhe para a câmara, por favor. Não sorria.
lines.en: Look at the camera, please. Don't smile.

dead_ends.text_en: Your photo shows a giant grin. Clerk: 'Muito simpático, mas outra vez.' (Very sweet, but again.)

side_scene.narration_en: Flash! The photo on the screen shows the biggest grin in AIMA history. The clerk turns the screen toward you, trying not to laugh.

lines.speaker: funcionária
lines.pt: Coloque o dedo aqui, por favor.

dead_ends.text_en: The clerk tries not to laugh: 'O pé não, o dedo!'

side_scene.narration_en: You start untying your shoe. The clerk waves both hands, laughing, and the whole waiting room turns to look.

pages.narration_en: All done. The clerk tells you what happens next.

lines.speaker: funcionária
lines.pt: Está concluído. Vai receber um e-mail.
lines.en: All done. You'll receive an email.

choices.text_en: Thank you! Have a good day!

dead_ends.text_en: The clerk is puzzled: 'De nada? Eu é que ajudei!' (I'm the one who helped!) To say thanks: obrigado (if you're a man) / obrigada (if you're a woman).

side_scene.narration_en: The clerk blinks, then laughs: 'De nada? Eu é que ajudei!' She thanks you back anyway, and you both end up thanking each other three times.

lines.speaker: funcionária
lines.pt: De nada? Eu é que ajudei!
lines.en: You're welcome? I'm the one who helped!

pages.narration_en: Celebration! You walk down to the Ribeira, with the Dom Luís I bridge in front of you, and sit at a riverside café. Either order is a happy ending.

lines.speaker: empregado
lines.en: Good afternoon! What would you like?

cafe.text_en: The coffee arrives, small, strong and perfect. You made it: you got through the AIMA appointment in Portuguese. Welcome to Porto!

francesinha.text_en: A steaming francesinha lands on your table, the most Porto thing you could order. You earned it. Welcome to Porto!
